newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN LEADS AFTER FIRST LEG.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN LEADS AFTER FIRST LEG.

text.p: Switzerland's Michael von Gruenigen posted the fastest time in the first leg of an Alpine skiing World Cup giant slalom on Tuesday.
Von Gruenigen, looking for his third successive win and a sweep of the giant slalom classics, twisted his way down the sun-drenched Kuonisbergli course in a time one minute 10.31 seconds.
The 27-year-old Swiss will start the second run (1200 GMT) with a wafer-thin 0.12 seconds advantage over Austria's Hans Knaus who clocked the second-best time of 1:10.43.
Knaus was followed closely by team mate Rainer Salzgeber (1:10.59) as Austrian's dominated the first leg recording four of the top six times.

Norway's Lasse Kjus, the reigning overall World Cup champion, returned to competition for the first time since the circuit moved to Europe in December and posted the eighth-best time of the first run.
Italy's Alberto Tomba, still bothered by the flu that forced him out of the second leg of the slalom in Chamonix on Sunday, did not race.
World champion Tomba could now tumble out of the top 15 in the giant slalom rankings for the first time in 10-years.
